evidence: update-order.service.ts: UpdateOrderService injects OrdersRepository from 'src/delivery/orders/dal/orders.repository' and uses UpdateOrderDto from 'src/delivery/orders/dtos', returning Promise<Order>. This is an orders-module concern placed in deliveryman/services.

update-deliverymans-orders.service.ts: deliverymanWithOrders.addNewMessageToOrders(description) vs update-order.service.ts: order.addInfoToDescription(description). Two separate paths add text to an order's description.
update-deliverymans-info.service.ts: directly assigns deliverymanWithOrders.firstName / lastName, while the other services use aggregate methods (changeStatus, addOrder, addNewMessageToOrders).

add-order-to-deliveryman, change-deliverymans-status, find-all-deliverymans, update-deliverymans-info, update-deliverymans-orders: `catch (error) { return error.message; }` returns a string typed as Deliveryman. create-deliveryman.service.ts and update-order.service.ts have no such handling.
update-deliverymans-info.service.ts and update-order.service.ts: `x !== undefined ?? (...)`. The left side is a boolean, so the right side never runs and the updates are silently skipped.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of the module is cohesive: deliveryman use cases that load the aggregate through DeliverymanRepository.findDeliverymanByIdWithOrders, call a domain method on Deliveryman, and save. update-order.service.ts breaks that. It is an Order use case that depends on the orders module's OrdersRepository and UpdateOrderDto, so it belongs to the orders concern, not here. Adding text to an order's description is also done in two places: UpdateDeliverymansOrdersService calls Deliveryman.addNewMessageToOrders, while UpdateOrderService calls Order.addInfoToDescription directly. update-deliverymans-info.service.ts skips the aggregate's own methods and assigns firstName/lastName directly, unlike its sibling services that call changeStatus or addOrder. Error handling is also inconsistent: five services catch errors and return error.message typed as Deliveryman, while create-deliveryman.service.ts and update-order.service.ts don't catch errors at all. Separately, the `x !== undefined ?? (...)` pattern in update-deliverymans-info.service.ts and update-order.service.ts never runs its right-hand side, because a boolean is never null or undefined. So those field updates never take effect.

violations.message: UpdateOrderService is an Order use case built on the orders module's OrdersRepository and UpdateOrderDto. It belongs to the orders concern, not the deliveryman services module. It also duplicates the 'append to order description' rule that UpdateDeliverymansOrdersService handles through Deliveryman.addNewMessageToOrders.

Skips the Deliveryman aggregate's own methods by assigning firstName/lastName directly, while sibling services go through domain methods. The `!== undefined ??` guard never runs its right-hand side, so the update is a no-op.
Holds a second path for adding descriptions to orders (addNewMessageToOrders), alongside Order.addInfoToDescription in update-order.service.ts. The order-description rule is not kept in one place.
